openings.claim: Switching may increase selection/checking time and errors.
openings.discriminator: Interleaving worsens these within layout/color/worker, without necessarily slowing insertion.
openings.probe: Counterbalance blocked/interleaved reusable samples for both workers; time four phases, verify contents, track wear; exclude accepted orders.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds switching; repeats already take 7–9 minutes.

openings.claim: Generic diagrams may obscure short-partition placement.
openings.discriminator: Order-specific diagrams reduce confusion with identical verified kits.
openings.probe: Compare two comparable five-person groups; record first placement, help, final arrangement; price diagrams.
openings.uncertainty: Ten participants screen interpretation, not pilot success.

openings.claim: Removable masks transfer positional guidance; inventory outlines separately expose missing/wrong pieces.
openings.discriminator: Placement and discrepancy detection improve independently of insertion speed.
openings.fit: Uncertain registration, removal, costs and schedule.
openings.probe: Hand-draw masks/outlines: 12 samples, six counterbalanced mixed-batch comparisons across counts/colors. Seed discrepancies; restore completeness. Time four phases plus preparation. Randomize customers 5/5; record completion/errors; measure costs/deadline impact.
openings.uncertainty: Needs verified parts lists, distinguishable parts, correspondence and usable instructions; benefits unproven.

decision: Screen D1 first; choose D2 or D3 within ten participants. Respect 15 samples, two workers/one bench, 500 initial/+0.40 per order; preserve 30×20 footprint/capacity, reversibility, counts/colors/deadline. Complaints do not establish packing omissions; width overlap supplies no threshold. Synthetic screens cannot establish pilot targets: 60 units, ≥98% complete, median ≤8 minutes, ≥90% unaided.
